chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Al-Reza (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Do not drive them out of their houses, nor should they themselves go forth, unless they commit an open indecency.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her hurting the family of the man and her evil manners.'

key_terms.فَاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ: An open, clear indecency or misconduct

ai.seo_question: What constitutes an 'open indecency' that allows a wife to leave her home according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) interprets the condition of 'open indecency' (fahisha mubinnah) in Surah At-Talaq not merely as sexual misconduct, but broadly to include causing distress to the husband's household and exhibiting poor character. This interpretation highlights the importance of domestic harmony and moral conduct in Shia jurisprudence, providing a nuanced understanding of the grounds for a wife's departure from the marital home.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>

regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [65:1] Do not drive them out of their houses, nor should they themselves go forth, unless they commit an open indecency. Heasws said: ‘Her hurting the family of the man and her evil manners’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “About the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, "... you must not send them out of their homes and they must not go out except if they commit an open indecent act’,
abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’It is a reference to her troubling the family of the man and her bad moral behavior.’”
